Subject: Partial responses + heavy retries observed since 15:30 UTC

Hi Ethan —

We started seeing increased partial responses and a series of retries from our worker fleet around 15:30 UTC today. Symptoms: repeated 500s during generation, some responses truncated mid-token, and our client has been issuing aggressive retries which amplified traffic.

We opened an internal ticket (ops-7241) and attached a short retry trace. Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing anything on your side or if there's an active incident? This is impacting our billing and a subset of API calls are taking 5–20s longer.

Hi Samantha — thanks for the report and the trace. We’re looking into it now.

Immediate notes:
- I’ve opened incident INC-20270315-RETRY and posted a preliminary entry on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-03-15-retry-failures
- Our edge telemetry shows a spike in retry attempts starting ~15:20 UTC correlating with a KV-cache invalidation event on a subset of inference nodes. That triggered our rate-limiting + retry paths to behave suboptimally for a small percentage of requests.

What we’re doing next (first-hour actions):
- We’re rolling a targeted configuration to reduce client-side retry amplification for affected customers and are enabling a short-term routing fallback to a stable model variant.
- I’ve attached a lightweight dump from our edge (incident-dump-20270315.log) for your ops team.

We’ll update this thread as we have mitigation progress. I understand the billing/latency concerns — if you need a short-term credit while we stabilize, I can escalate.

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-03-16T00:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Partial responses + heavy retries observed since 15:30 UTC

Internal: quick triage notes —
- Root cause (prelim): KV cache invalidation on a subset of US-west inference hosts after a background compaction job. The invalidation caused a short window where kernel selection fell back and per-token latency spiked, which in turn tripped client-side retry logic for some customers.
- Mitigations applied:
  * Short-term routing fallback to stable pool (decreased p95 by ~320ms in canary).
  * Adjusted retry backoff threshold for affected tenant IDs (manual override).
  * Increasing KV cache warm-up threshold to avoid immediate invalidations during compactions.
- Next: fuller postmortem and permanent fix for compaction order and improved circuit breaking.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Ops

Subject: Post-incident summary: root cause & next steps (INC-20270315-RETRY)

Samantha / Holland Health team —

Thank you again for the quick trace and patience while we investigated. Short summary and next steps: 

Root cause (final): a background compaction job for our KV cache triggered aggressive eviction on ~3% of US-west inference hosts. That caused a temporary fallback to an execution kernel with higher per-token latency. The increased latency triggered a retry amplification pattern in some client setups which produced the partial responses you observed.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Targeted routing to stable pool completed 01:48 UTC (reduced retries in canary & full roll by 02:30 UTC).
- Manual retry-backoff override for affected tenant IDs.
- Short-term credit offered: we will apply a one-time usage credit for the affected window — Marissa will follow up with details.

Planned permanent fixes:
- Harden compaction ordering to avoid evicting warm prefixes (engineering change in Q2 release).
- Improve circuit-breaker sensitivity to avoid synchronous retries across worker fleets.
- Enhance observability: new alert for KV eviction rate + automated routing rollback.

Public incident page and timeline: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-03-15-retry-failures
Internal postmortem draft (shared tomorrow): https://drive.redwood.ai/open?id=1A2b3C-retry-trace

If you’d like a quick sync with our engineering lead to go over the postmortem, we can schedule a 30-min call next week.

Ethan
Ethan Park
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident-dump-20270315.log; retry-trace-20270315.json
